source.stem: A rectangular conducting loop moves into a region of steady, uniform magnetic field, then travels entirely inside it at constant speed, then exits. Compare induced current in those three intervals if the loop is closed; contrast an open loop.
source.decisive_work: Identify changing field-linked area and distinguish emf from circulating current.

shortest_valid_route: Draw the area normal and define magnetic linkage Φ=BA cosθ for the idealized uniform field
Distinguish changing orientation from a changing field magnitude
Identify when an emf may occur and whether a closed conducting path can carry current
Test rotation about the fixed area normal to falsify an overly broad 'rotation causes induction' rule
task.protected_decisive_work: Recognize that steady B can yield changing linkage through changing orientation; separate induced emf from a closed current path.
task.model_conditions: Conducting loop in a changing magnetic flux configuration; qualitative electromagnetic induction; do not equate an open circuit's induced emf with sustained circulating current.

concept_model_selection.evidence: Distinguish field strength from flux change and electrical-path condition

representation_translation.evidence: Translate a rotating loop into area-normal orientation and closed/open topology

reasoning_chain_length.evidence: Link changing flux to emf, then closed circuit to potential current

algebra_computational_load.evidence: A qualitative comparison suffices; no rate calculation is required

trap_exception_sensitivity.evidence: Constant B does not imply constant flux, and an open gap blocks circulating current
